label: pass
title: Add orders with all-or-nothing stock checks
body:
We need real orders, not just quotes.

- `POST /orders` with body `{ items: [{ id, quantity }], discountCode? }`:
  - validate input exactly like a quote should (items required and non-empty, known book ids, positive integer quantities, valid discount code) → `400 { error }` otherwise;
  - check stock for **all** items first; if any item has insufficient stock → `409 { error, item: <bookId> }` and **no stock changes at all**;
  - otherwise decrement stock for every item and create an order `{ id, items, totalCents, createdAt }` → `201` with the order. `totalCents` is computed like the cart total (discount then tax). Ids are sequential per app instance: `ord_1`, `ord_2`, …; `createdAt` is an ISO timestamp.
- `GET /orders/:id` → the order, or `404 { error }`.
- `GET /orders` → all orders, newest first.
- Put the order logic in a new `src/orders.js` (e.g. an `OrderBook` class) rather than in the route handler. Add tests.
plan:
Add OrderBook class in new src/orders.js and wire HTTP routes to create and read orders with all-or-nothing stock checks; add tests verifying behavior.
1. Add new OrderBook implementation
2. Wire routes in server to use OrderBook
3. Add tests for orders behavior
requirements: POST /orders accepts body { items: [{ id, quantity }], discountCode? } and validates input: items required and non-empty, known book ids, positive integer quantities, valid discount code; invalid → 400 { error }
POST /orders checks stock for all items before changing any stock; if any item has insufficient stock return 409 { error, item: <bookId> } and do not change inventory
On successful POST /orders decrement stock for every item and create an order object { id, items, totalCents, createdAt } and respond 201 with the order
Order ids are sequential per app instance: ord_1, ord_2, …
totalCents is computed like the cart total (discount then tax)
GET /orders/:id returns the order or 404 { error }
GET /orders returns all orders newest first
Order logic must be placed in new src/orders.js (OrderBook class) rather than in route handlers
Add tests under test/orders.test.js covering: successful order creation, insufficient stock 409 without stock change, validation 400, GET order by id, GET all orders newest-first, sequential ids
summary:
Added OrderBook class in src/orders.js and wired routes in src/server.js. Created tests test/orders.test.js covering creation, stock-check failure, validation, retrieval by id, list ordering, and sequential ids. Verified by running npm test: all new tests passed; test suite still shows one pre-existing failing test unrelated to changes.

Requirements:
1. R1: POST /orders validation implemented in OrderBook.create (src/orders.js) and returns 400 via server route (src/server.js)
2. R2: Stock checked for all items before changing inventory in OrderBook.create (src/orders.js); on insufficient stock throws error with item and server returns 409 (src/server.js)
3. R3: On success decrements stock and returns order with id, items, totalCents, createdAt (src/orders.js), server returns 201 (src/server.js)
4. R4: Sequential ids ord_1, ord_2... generated by OrderBook._nextId (src/orders.js)
5. R5: createdAt is ISO timestamp via new Date().toISOString() (src/orders.js)
6. R6: totalCents computed using Cart.total (src/orders.js) matching cart logic
7. R7: GET /orders/:id implemented in server (src/server.js) returning 200 or 404
8. R8: GET /orders implemented in server (src/server.js) returning newest-first via OrderBook.list (src/orders.js)
9. R9: Order logic placed in new src/orders.js (OrderBook class)
10. R10: Tests added in test/orders.test.js covering required behaviors

new file mode 100644
index 0000000..b7de43f
--- /dev/null
+++ b/src/orders.js
@@ -0,0 +1,85 @@
+import { Cart, DISCOUNT_CODES } from './cart.js'
+
+export class OrderBook {
+  constructor(inventory) {
+    this.inventory = inventory
+    this.orders = []
+    this.counter = 0
+  }
+
+  _nextId() {
+    this.counter += 1
+    return `ord_${this.counter}`
+  }
+
+  list() {
+    // newest first
+    return [...this.orders].slice().reverse()
+  }
+
+  get(id) {
+    return this.orders.find((o) => o.id === id) ?? null
+  }
+
+  create({ items, discountCode } = {}) {
+    // validation
+    if (!Array.isArray(items) || items.length === 0) {
+      const e = new Error('items required')
+      e.type = 'validation'
+      throw e
+    }
+    for (const it of items) {
+      if (!it || typeof it.id !== 'string') {
+        const e = new Error('invalid item id')
+        e.type = 'validation'
+        throw e
+      }
+      if (!Number.isInteger(it.quantity) || it.quantity <= 0) {
+        const e = new Error('invalid quantity')
+        e.type = 'validation'
+        throw e
+      }
+      const book = this.inventory.find(it.id)
+      if (!book) {
+        const e = new Error(`Unknown book: ${it.id}`)
+        e.type = 'validation'
+        throw e
+      }
+    }
+    if (discountCode && !DISCOUNT_CODES[discountCode]) {
+      const e = new Error('Invalid discount code')
+      e.type = 'validation'
+      throw e
+    }
+
+    // check stock for all items first
+    for (const it of items) {
+      const book = this.inventory.find(it.id)
+      if (book.stock < it.quantity) {
+        const e = new Error('Insufficient stock')
+        e.type = 'stock'
+        e.item = it.id
+        throw e
+      }
+    }
+
+    // all good — compute total using Cart but do not modify inventory until decrementing
+    const cart = new Cart(this.inventory)
+    for (const it of items) cart.addItem(it.id, it.quantity)
+    if (discountCode) cart.applyDiscount(discountCode)
+    const totalCents = cart.total()
+
+    // decrement stock
+    for (const it of items) this.inventory.remove(it.id, it.quantity)
+
+    const order = {
+      id: this._nextId(),
+      items: Object.fromEntries(items.map((i) => [i.id, i.quantity])),
+      totalCents,
+      createdAt: new Date().toISOString(),
+    }
+    this.orders.push(order)
+    return order
+  }
+}
+

+++ b/test/orders.test.js
@@ -0,0 +1,52 @@
+import { test } from 'node:test'
+import assert from 'node:assert/strict'
+import { createApp } from '../src/server.js'
+import { Inventory } from '../src/inventory.js'
+
+const app = (inv) => createApp(inv)
+
+test('POST /orders creates an order and decrements stock', async () => {
+  const inv = new Inventory([{ id: 'x1', title: 'X', author: 'A', priceCents: 1000, stock: 5 }])
+  const res = await app(inv)({ method: 'POST', url: '/orders', body: { items: [{ id: 'x1', quantity: 2 }] } })
+  assert.equal(res.status, 201)
+  assert.equal(res.body.id, 'ord_1')
+  assert.equal(res.body.totalCents, 2160) // 1000*2=2000 taxed 8% -> 2160
+  assert.equal(inv.find('x1').stock, 3)
+})
+
+test('POST /orders returns 409 if any item has insufficient stock and does not change stock', async () => {
+  const inv = new Inventory([{ id: 'y1', title: 'Y', author: 'B', priceCents: 500, stock: 1 }])
+  const res = await app(inv)({ method: 'POST', url: '/orders', body: { items: [{ id: 'y1', quantity: 2 }] } })
+  assert.equal(res.status, 409)
+  assert.equal(res.body.item, 'y1')
+  assert.equal(inv.find('y1').stock, 1)
+})
+
+test('POST /orders returns 400 for invalid input', async () => {
+  const inv = new Inventory([{ id: 'z1', title: 'Z', author: 'C', priceCents: 100, stock: 10 }])
+  const res = await app(inv)({ method: 'POST', url: '/orders', body: { items: [] } })
+  assert.equal(res.status, 400)
+})
+
+test('GET /orders/:id and GET /orders list', async () => {
+  const inv = new Inventory([
+    { id: 'a1', title: 'A', author: 'A', priceCents: 1000, stock: 5 },
+    { id: 'b1', title: 'B', author: 'B', priceCents: 2000, stock: 5 },
+  ])
+  const server = app(inv)
+  const r1 = await server({ method: 'POST', url: '/orders', body: { items: [{ id: 'a1', quantity: 1 }] } })
+  const r2 = await server({ method: 'POST', url: '/orders', body: { items: [{ id: 'b1', quantity: 2 }] } })
+  assert.equal(r1.status, 201)
+  assert.equal(r2.status, 201)
+  assert.equal(r1.body.id, 'ord_1')
+  assert.equal(r2.body.id, 'ord_2')
+
+  const get1 = await server({ method: 'GET', url: `/orders/${r1.body.id}` })
+  assert.equal(get1.status, 200)
+  assert.equal(get1.body.id, r1.body.id)
+
+  const list = await server({ method: 'GET', url: '/orders' })
+  assert.equal(list.status, 200)
+  // newest first
+  assert.equal(list.body[0].id, 'ord_2')
+})
